rubric.why: This states the defining amount of solute and the volume of solution used for m/v percentage.
rubric.description: Defines m/v percentage as the mass of solute in 100 cm³ of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the mass of solute, in grams, present in 100 cm³ of solution.

rubric.why: The formula expresses the mass-to-volume proportion as a percentage.
rubric.description: Gives the formula for m/v percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula, including multiplication by 100.

modelAnswer: Mass/volume percentage is the mass of solute, in grams, dissolved in 100 cm3 of solution.
m/v % = (mass of solute in g / volume of solution in cm3) × 100.

items.followUp: What are strong electrolytes? Give one example.

rubric.why: Partial ionization in solution is the defining feature of a weak electrolyte.
rubric.description: States that weak electrolytes ionize only partially in aqueous solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that only some of the dissolved substance forms ions.

rubric.why: A valid example completes the response.
rubric.description: Gives one example of a weak electrolyte.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example, such as acetic acid.

modelAnswer: Weak electrolytes ionize only partially in aqueous solution.

items.followUp: State four postulates of Dalton’s atomic theory.

rubric.why: Bohr proposed that electrons occupy definite permitted orbits around the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that electrons revolve around the nucleus in fixed orbits or energy levels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the permitted fixed orbits or energy levels.

rubric.why: Electrons in permitted stationary orbits do not continuously lose or gain energy.
rubric.description: States that an electron in a permitted orbit does not radiate or absorb energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this stationary-orbit property.

rubric.why: Only certain orbits are allowed, as expressed by the quantization of angular momentum.
rubric.description: States that angular momentum is quantized, or gives the corresponding relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the quantization rule or giving mvr = nh/2π.

rubric.why: The energy of permitted orbits increases with their distance from the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that orbit energy increases with distance from the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship between orbit distance and energy.

rubric.why: An electron exchanges a definite amount of energy when it transitions between permitted orbits.
rubric.description: Explains that an electron absorbs or emits energy during a transition between orbits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing absorption or emission during a transition, or giving ΔE = hν.

modelAnswer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in fixed circular orbits called energy levels or shells.
An electron in a permitted orbit does not radiate or absorb energy; its energy remains constant.
Only certain orbits are allowed, and the electron’s angular momentum is quantized: mvr = nh/2π.
The energy of an orbit increases as its distance from the nucleus increases.
An electron absorbs or emits a definite amount of energy when it jumps between orbits; ΔE = hν.

items.followUp: Write four physical properties of metals.

rubric.why: Lack of lustre is a common physical property of non-metals.
rubric.description: States that non-metals are generally dull or non-lustrous.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for dullness or lack of lustre.

rubric.why: Solid non-metals are generally brittle rather than malleable or ductile.
rubric.description: States that solid non-metals are brittle.

accept: poor conductors of heat and electricity
rubric.why: Non-metals generally conduct heat and electricity poorly.
rubric.description: States that non-metals are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for poor conductivity of heat and electricity.

rubric.why: Low melting and boiling points are common physical properties of non-metals.
rubric.description: Gives a further physical property: generally low melting or boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that non-metals generally have low melting points or low boiling points.

modelAnswer: Non-metals are generally dull and non-lustrous.
They are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity.
They generally have low melting and boiling points.
